title: Make zstd:chunked compressor reproducible.
body:
tar reader is returning time.Time values with local timezone attached. Compressor was serializing these values to json, which also saved timezones, e.g. "2023-01-01T01:00:00+01:00".

comments.body:
> Note that the compression implementation makes no promises to be reproducible (and the implementation is changing ~every month); so, ultimately, reproducibility is at best an accidental outcome, not a possible design goal (without changing the used compression library or, extremely unlikely, us maintaining one).

Maybe I'm using wrong term here. I do not expect format to stay stable across versions.

But rules_img needs to be able to re-run same binary on the same input tar and get same output. Which should be the case after .UTC() fix.

I understand that you do not want to make promises regarding deterministic behavior, but shouldn't it be a stated goal of tooling that creates blobs for OCI images to be as close to a pure function as possible?
Everything else leads to inefficiencies (like writing the same content into a layer on two different occasions, but having to store it in a container registry twice because some bits of the encoded blobs differ).

> the implementation is changing ~every month

Apologies for hijacking this thread, but do those changes include the specification of the on-disk representation of `zstd:chunked`?
Also, if determinism is a requirement, would you recommend against using this library (or `zstd:chunked` in general)?

> But rules_img needs to be able to re-run same binary on the same input tar and get same output.

AFAIK the compression implementation we use does not promise that.

>> But rules_img needs to be able to re-run same binary on the same input tar and get same output.
>
> AFAIK the compression implementation we use does not promise that.

I rechecked, looks like it [does](https://github.com/klauspost/compress/blob/v1.20.3/zstd/README.md#future-compatibility-guarantees).

> The Encoder can be assumed to produce the same output from the exact same code version. However, the may be modes in the future that break this, although they will not be enabled without an explicit option.

> shouldn't it be a stated goal of tooling that creates blobs for OCI images to be as close to a pure function as possible?

Sure, that would be nice. But being able to make it a goal seems to require us signing up to maintain a compression library (which we are definitely unable/unwilling to do, given the amount of changes in `github.com/klauspost/compress`), or finding some other compression library that is stable that way (at an acceptable performance cost?).

For comparison, although the gzip format is much older and much better-understood, we have seen the Go standard library’s `gzip` output changing at least two (three?) times, most recently https://tip.golang.org/doc/go1.27#compressflatepkgcompressflate .

> > the implementation is changing ~every month
> 
> Apologies for hijacking this thread, but do those changes include the specification of the on-disk representation of `zstd:chunked`?

I meant the pace of change of `github.com/klauspost/compress`. The format specification, is, AFAIK, stable, and all such output should be interoperable. (We did have some breaking changes in the early days of `zstd:chunked`, and we hope not to have any more, although #681 will probably eventually happen.)

> Also, if determinism is a requirement, would you recommend against using this library (or `zstd:chunked` in general)?

With the understanding that we can’t _promise_ long-term reproducibility, this is ultimately an empirical question. I don’t know that anyone has been collecting such data on the reproducibility of the outputs. @giuseppe might very well know something I don’t.

> > AFAIK the compression implementation we use does not promise that.
> 
> I rechecked, looks like it [does](https://github.com/klauspost/compress/blob/v1.20.3/zstd/README.md#future-compatibility-guarantees).
> 
> > The Encoder can be assumed to produce the same output from the exact same code version. However, the may be modes in the future that break this, although they will not be enabled without an explicit option.

That’s interesting, thanks!

the code change LGTM, I am not sure either if we can achieve reproducibility of the compressed stream, but we are looking at reproducibility for the uncompressed stream: https://github.com/composefs/composefs-rs/pull/356
